rationale: The core problem — Google's Outdated Content tool returning false negatives — is a Google-side bug that Google could fix at any time, making any tooling built around it ephemeral and unreliable as a business. The buyer (SEO agency or consultant) is identifiable and does pay for tools, but this specific problem is infrequent enough per client that willingness to pay for a dedicated solution is questionable; most would expect a workaround blog post rather than a paid service. At 4.1, it falls below the validate threshold of 5.5.
solution_plan: Not recommended. The problem is entirely dependent on a Google tool that may be fixed or further broken at any time — there is no stable surface to build on. SEO practitioners would be the buyer, but the frequency is too low and the addressable market too diffuse for a viable micro-service. Pass.
notes: Below validate threshold (4.1 < 5.5). No build gates tested.
